_README: Worked example of the two halves of one delivery: a seller-signed x402 offer-receipt and the buyer-signed capacity-attest claim that answers it, joined by offerReceiptHash. Everything needed to check this offline is in this file. Both signatures are real. Verify with: node examples/verify-offer-receipt-link.mjs
signingKeyNote: Seller is the publicly known Hardhat/anvil account #1, buyer is account #0. TEST KEYS ONLY, never funded, never used for anything real. Published deliberately so this vector is reproducible by anyone.

sellerHalf._what: x402 offer-receipt extension artifact, signed by the resource server. Its payload carries no identifier of its own (spec section 5.2), which is why the buyer's claim references it by digest.
sellerHalf._typesNote: Recorded here for offline verification only. The spec (section 3.2.1) says these are normative and MUST NOT be transmitted on the wire.

buyerHalf._what: capacity-attest delivery claim, signed by the buyer. delivered is 'partial': the seller's receipt says service was delivered, the buyer says 25230 of 28800 gpu-seconds arrived. Both statements can be true at once, which is the entire reason both halves are kept.

theJoin._what: sha256 over sellerHalf.transmittedBytes, carried inside the buyer's signed content. Because it is inside the signed bytes, changing it changes claimId and breaks the buyer's signature, so a receipt reference cannot be swapped in or stripped out after the fact.
theJoin._signerNote: True here because this example uses the spec's simplest signer-authorization approach, where the service signs with the key for its payTo address. The spec says production deployments SHOULD use a dedicated signing key instead, in which case the recovered receipt signer will NOT equal sellerAddress and this equality must not be relied on.

whatThisVectorDoesNotEstablish: That the receipt signer was authorized to speak for the service. The spec treats signer authorization as a separate, external problem (section 4.3 on authorization approaches) and notes it SHOULD be evaluated as of the receipt's issuedAt, not at verification time. Nothing here checks that.
That the settlement transaction exists or moved any funds. These are unfunded test keys and no chain was consulted.
That the delivered amounts are accurate. The buyer asserts them; capacity-attest records the assertion and who signed it, and never certifies that an assertion is true.
Any judgment about whether the seller performed well. There is no score here, only two signed statements and the link between them.
